paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: (left) and (right) of scaling up SFT dataset across various model scales in the LLaMA-2 family. The results suggest scaling up model scales and SFT dataset can further improve .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three variants of the LLaMA-2 model—LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B—on the CoLeG-E metric (expressed as a percentage) under different Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) conditions. The horizontal axis lists the three model sizes in increasing order of parameter count, while the vertical axis represents the CoLeG-E score ranging from 0 to 50%, with major tick marks at intervals of 10%. For each model, four grouped bars are shown, corresponding to different SFT configurations: "no SFT" (light blue with diagonal stripes), "+ SFT on D₀" (light orange with horizontal stripes), "+ SFT on D₀, D₁" (light purple with diagonal stripes), and "+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂" (light red with no pattern). Performance increases with each additional dataset used for SFT across all model sizes. For LLaMA-2-7B, scores rise from approximately 5% (no SFT) to about 32% (SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂). For LLaMA-2-13B, scores increase from roughly 9% to about 39%. For LLaMA-2-70B, scores grow from around 26% to approximately 50%. The chart visually demonstrates that both increasing model size and expanding the SFT dataset lead to higher CoLeG-E scores, with the largest model (70B) achieving the highest performance under the most comprehensive SFT setting.
